About the Role

As a Principal Recommendation System/Platform Engineer, you will lead the upgrade of our core recommendation architecture and recommendation model platform, transforming our existing rule-based personalization system into an industrial-grade, large-scale, real-time ML recommendation platform. This role spans key business scenarios, including trading products, content feeds, the community, and AI-powered investment workflows such as TradeGPT.
You will work closely with recommendation algorithm, growth product and operations, and data science teams to build a high-throughput, low-latency, highly available foundation for personalization at scale, serving more than 80 million users globally. You will lead architectural decisions, infrastructure development, and end-to-end delivery, taking the platform from zero to one in a resource-constrained, fast-moving environment.

Key Responsibilities

Develop high-throughput, low-latency recommendation services. Continuously improve system performance and reliability, and establish robust degradation and disaster-recovery mechanisms.
Build and optimize large-scale model training infrastructure, including distributed training, job scheduling, resource management, fault recovery, and training observability. Improve training efficiency, stability, and resource utilization.
Build model deployment capabilities and high-performance online inference services. Optimize model loading, inference latency, throughput, and infrastructure cost; implement autoscaling, canary releases, graceful degradation, and disaster recovery to ensure service availability under high traffic.
Establish an engineering feedback loop from offline evaluation and online experimentation to production monitoring. Monitor model quality, service performance, and anomalies; build alerting capabilities to support incident diagnosis and safe rollback.
Collaborate with recommendation algorithm and business engineering teams to identify common needs across trading products, content feeds, community, and other recommendation scenarios. Standardize training, deployment, and inference capabilities to bring models into production reliably and efficiently.

Major Requirements

At least 4 years of recommender systems engineering experience at a consumer-facing internet company. You have contributed substantially to the design and development of a model training platform, model deployment platform, or large-scale online inference service, and have hands-on experience resolving production issues.
Strong computer science fundamentals and proficiency in at least one of Go, Java, or C++. You write well-structured code, apply sound design principles, and enjoy tackling challenging engineering problems.
Familiarity with at least one mainstream deep learning framework, such as PyTorch or TensorFlow. You understand the end-to-end workflow of training, exporting, deploying, and serving recommendation models, and have practical experience with distributed training or training job orchestration.
An understanding of the recommendation system lifecycle and the engineering considerations involved in sequence models, multi-objective models, and other recommender model types. You can work with algorithm teams to turn model requirements into reusable, maintainable production platform capabilities.
Experience designing and optimizing high-throughput, low-latency services. You can diagnose and resolve online inference issues involving throughput, P99 latency, reliability, and resource cost.

Nice-to-have:

Architecture experience in search, advertising, or recommendations at major technology companies
Experience leading the development of a training platform, model deployment platform, or online inference pipeline from the ground up in a large-scale recommendation, advertising, or search system, and making those capabilities reusable across business scenarios.
Experience optimizing distributed training or inference for complex recommendation models, or scheduling heterogeneous CPU/GPU resources.
Experience with cross-region high-availability deployments, active-active architectures, model release governance, or large-scale production incident response.
An AI-driven approach and hands-on experience bringing LLM or agent applications into production for search, advertising, or recommendation use cases.

Why Join Us

A multi-domain recommendation challenge in fintech:
Go beyond a single domain such as video or e-commerce. You will build personalization capabilities across trading products, market intelligence, community content, campaigns, and AI-powered investment workflows.
Proven business impact with substantial room for ML advancement:
Our current recommendation system has demonstrated a 71% increase in CTR and a 1,285% increase in conversion rate, with significant potential for an ML-native upgrade.
Work at the intersection of AI and recommendations:
Build where traditional recommender systems, generative AI, and LLM agents meet—one of the most active frontiers in engineering.
An opportunity to lead, not just follow:
Our combination of trading, content, community, AI, and campaigns creates distinctive technical challenges and enables rapid iteration.
Global scale:
Serve more than 80 million users across over 200 countries, tackling the real-world complexity of large-scale, real-time systems.

jobs.description:
About Xage

Cyberattacks on critical infrastructure, government, and private enterprises are at an all time high – and only growing more urgent with AI. Xage is a global leader in zero trust access and protection at the forefront of solving this pressing issue. We are pioneering a secure tomorrow by empowering organizations worldwide to connect anyone to anything, while delivering unparalleled defense against every cyber threat.

We have built tremendous momentum across governments and commercial enterprises around the world, and it’s just the beginning. Recognized by Forbes as one of America’s Best Startup Employers, Xage prioritizes creativity, collaboration, and innovation in pursuit of our mission.
We are headquartered in Palo Alto, CA and have global teams across North America, EMEA, and APJ.

We’re passionate about solving problems that have positive, real-world consequences for the lives of everyday people. We hope you’ll join us in the fight against cyberattacks and safeguarding critical systems.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced and visionary Senior Software Engineer
to design and build our next-generation Zero Trust for Agentic AI
platform. As AI agents evolve from sandboxed pilots into autonomous systems capable of executing real-world actions, invoking APIs, and accessing sensitive databases across hybrid cloud and operational technology (OT) environments, security must evolve with them.
In this role, you will build the critical security fabric that moves past simple prompt/output monitoring and into deterministic runtime visibility and control
. You will engineer the gateways, proxies, and identity management systems that protect autonomous AI agents, Large Language Models (LLMs), and enterprise resources from prompt injection, rogue behavior, data leakage, and privilege escalation.

Key Responsibilities

Architect AI Gateways & Sentries:
Design and develop the runtime components (like Xage Agent Sentry and Resource Gateway) to encapsulate AI agents, intercepting and inspecting inputs, outputs, tool calls, and API interactions.
Implement Deterministic Access Controls:
Build jailbreak-proof, identity-based permissioning models and agent entitlements to enforce strict least-privilege access across APIs, SaaS applications, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and databases.
Analyze Behavioral Anomalies:
Build intelligent monitoring systems that establish a baseline for normal agent behavior and leverage ML to flag deviations, catching rogue agent actions or privilege escalation attempts before they hit critical infrastructure.
Develop Agent Identity Management:
Create robust, centralized frameworks for agent registration, lifecycle management, and automated credential rotation to eliminate hardcoded secrets and shared service account vulnerabilities.
Build End-to-End Visibility Pipelines:
Engineer high-throughput, tamperproof logging mechanisms to capture and audit every prompt, action, tool call, and resource access for comprehensive governance.
Scale a Distributed Security Fabric:
Ensure security controls deploy seamlessly across multi-cloud, on-premises, and edge/OT environments via a unified, resilient platform.

Required Skills and Qualifications

Technical Requirements

Backend & Systems Engineering:
3-5+ years of experience building high-performance, distributed, and scalable enterprise software (preferred languages: Go, Python, C or C++).
Machine Learning & AI Security:
Strong hands-on experience deploying ML models in production environments. Familiarity with NLP, LLM alignment/guardrails (e.g., Llama Guard, NeMo Guardrails), and implementing low-latency inference at the proxy/gateway level.
AI/LLM Integration & Protocols:
Deep understanding of the Agentic AI lifecycle, tool-calling mechanisms, and emerging integration protocols like MCP (Model Context Protocol)
and REST APIs.
Security & Zero Trust Architecture:
Solid foundation in application security, API gateway design, proxy architectures (e.g., Envoy), identity access management (IAM), and credential management/rotation.
Infrastructure & Edge:
Experience with containerization (Docker, Kubernetes) and deploying applications across hybrid environments (Cloud, SaaS, and Edge/OT).

Soft Skills & Experience

Experience in cybersecurity product development, specifically in AI Security (Securing LLMs/Agents, prompt injection mitigation) is highly preferred.
Strong systems-level thinking with the ability to build predictive boundaries around dynamic, runtime AI behaviors.
Strong communication skills to collaborate with AI researchers, security analysts, and enterprise architecture teams.

Key Business Impacts You Will Deliver

Enable High-Stakes AI Deployment:
Turn risky, sandboxed AI experiments into secure, production-ready enterprise tools.
Mitigate Modern Threats:
Directly block harmful agent behaviors and data exfiltration before they impact the business.
Simplify AI Complexity:
Provide enterprises with a “single pane of glass” view to trust, govern, and audit their autonomous AI workforces.

jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Reinforcement learning is how Claude learns to reason, write code, and act autonomously over long horizons. new_jobs.description:
Position Description

The Senior AI/ML Engineer is responsible for building and operating the foundation that puts AI to work across the organization: the Azure infrastructure AI workloads run on, the patterns every engineering team uses to develop with agents, and UNOS’s own production agents.

UNOS will be building everything from conventional machine learning models to generative AI workflows to more autonomous agentic solutions; this role makes them run in production, safe for protected health information by default, with evaluation, monitoring, and cost under control.

This role requires a strong background in cloud /infrastructure engineering and the ability to apply that expertise to AI technologies while continuing to advance AI capabilities across UNOS. This role provides an opportunity to shape the trajectory of AI and agentic development and make a real difference in people’s lives, in a domain spanning healthcare, logistics, clinical science, and biotech.

Key Responsibilities

Provision AI infrastructure on Azure as code, including model deployments in Microsoft Foundry and Databricks, GPU capacity, agent runtimes, as well as the networking, identity, and secrets around them.
Stand up open-weight and frontier models on UNOS infrastructure under a pattern approved by Security and Privacy for protected health information (PHI).
Develop the technical policies and build controls into the platform itself: per-agent identities, least-privilege access, private endpoints, allow-listed models, and audit evidence produced as a byproduct of normal use.
Run shared model access across providers, with routing, quotas, tracing, and cost attributed to each team and use case.
Build sandboxed environments where engineers run coding agents against real repositories, with no production credentials inside.
Define UNOS’s standard patterns for agentic development and publish them as working templates and reference implementations.
Integrate AI into CI/CD for pull-request review, test-failure triage, and security findings.
Build and ship UNOS’s own agents, in UNOS One products and for internal operations, including tool access, retrieval, orchestration, and human approval where a decision requires it.
Build the path from prototype to production in UNOS One, so a working proof of concept ships without being rebuilt.
Own evaluation and release for agents and conventional models alike, including test sets, staged rollout, rollback, and monitoring.
Baseline and track the time from idea to working proof of concept, and the quality of what ships.
Teach agentic development across UNOS through pairing, working sessions, and code review, and mentoring engineers in the AI function.
Recommend build-or-buy decisions on AI platforms and tools, with cost and risk stated.
Perform other duties and support additional administrative priorities as assigned, consistent with the general scope and level of the position.

Minimum Requirements

Approximately six (6) years of experience building and running production systems, including at least three (3) years owning cloud infrastructure as code.

Critical Skills

Production cloud depth, Azure preferred (equivalent AWS or GCP experience considered), with Terraform or Bicep: virtual networks, private endpoints, managed identities, role-based access, secrets, and policy.
Strong handle on fundamental principles of AI/ML (e.g. train/test/validation, overfitting, calibration, eval methods)
Hands-on provisioning of AI workloads, including model serving endpoints, quota and capacity, GPU compute, and cost controls.
An LLM-based system built and run in production, past the demo stage, including tool calling or agents, retrieval, evaluation, and tracing.
Experience working under HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2, FedRAMP, or a similar control framework, translating controls into configuration and evidence.
Daily practice with coding agents such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, or Cursor.

Building leading software ahead of the curve to accelerate and improve cybersecurity tooling for AI.
Collaborating closely with research teams and product teams to be responsible for development of research code into alpha versions of products.
Rapidly identifying the highest-value MVP for ambiguous security and identity problems, prototyping solutions, validating them with partner teams, and iterating towards production-ready services.
Developing reusable skills, CLI tools, APIs, and integration patterns to help internal teams embrace secure agent approaches across enterprise tools and platforms.
Partnering closely with teams across Enterprise Security, Product Security, Enterprise AI, Enterprise Product, and relevant platform teams to align architecture with real workflow needs and operational constraints.

Experience with multi-contributor software projects and long-running software projects.
Familiarity with building agents, AI tooling, and architectures.
Track record of framing problem spaces, defining an MVP, prototyping quickly, and evolving ideas into production systems.

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Reinforcement learning is how Claude learns to reason, write code, and act autonomously over long horizons. At frontier scale, an RL run is a large distributed system: training, sampling, and environment execution run concurrently across a large fleet of accelerators and hosts. As an engineer in RL Engineering, you'll work on keeping that system secure as it scales.

This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll work in the RL codebase and the infrastructure underneath it, alongside the engineers and researchers who build and use it. The system is large and changes as fast as the research does, so security work here has to keep up with that pace without costing performance or velocity.

We're hiring from two backgrounds: security engineers who want to work on large-scale ML systems, and ML systems or research engineers who want to work on security. Strong candidates have depth in one and real interest in the other.

Key responsibilities

Design, build, and operate security controls for RL training systems and the infrastructure they run on
Work across the stack (orchestration, environments, training, inference) wherever the work is needed
Review designs and code across the RL stack, find security problems, and fix them
Build shared libraries and tooling that other RL engineers and researchers build on
Build the observability needed to understand what these systems are doing
Work with researchers and performance engineers to make sure security changes preserve training correctness and performance
Write clear design documents for what you build

Minimum Qualifications

Strong software engineering skills in Python and at least one systems language such as Rust, C++, or Go
Experience designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems or security systems in production
Strong understanding of security fundamentals
Working knowledge of Linux, containers, and cloud infrastructure
Experience debugging complex problems across many hosts and services
Ability to reason about tradeoffs between security, performance, and reliability
Strong written communication, including design documents

Preferred Qualifications

Experience running ML training or inference infrastructure at scale
Experience with infrastructure security, such as isolation, access control, networking, or identity
Experience with container orchestration such as Kubernetes, and with sandboxed or virtualized code execution at scale
Experience building observability for large fleets
Experience supporting research teams or other fast-moving internal users
Familiarity with reinforcement learning or large language model training workloads

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

You’ll own the agent harnesses that turn model capabilities into useful actions: planning, tool execution, context management, memory, and error recovery.

You will work closely with product, design, and engineering to build agents that research accounts, identify opportunities, and execute GTM workflows. You’ll move quickly from prototype to customer usage, then use evaluations and real execution traces to make the product better. If you want to build production AI systems and own the outcome from first experiment through launch, this role is for you.

What You’ll Do:

Build agent harnesses: Design the execution loops, tool interfaces, context, and memory that let agents complete complex workflows reliably.
Ship AI products end to end: Turn ambiguous customer problems into working features, connecting agents to Unify’s data, integrations, and workflow infrastructure.
Make quality measurable: Build evals from real customer tasks, and use traces and failure analysis to improve agent behavior.
Build for production: Own reliability, latency, and cost. Make long-running tasks resumable, handle tool failures, and give users visibility and control over agent actions.
Experiment with new capabilities: Test models, prompting strategies, retrieval approaches, and orchestration patterns. Measure what improves outcomes and bring it into the product.
Shape our AI foundation: Build reusable tools and engineering practices that help the team ship faster, partnering with product and design to prioritize the work that matters most to customers.

Who You Are:

You have 3+ years of software engineering experience and hands-on experience shipping LLM applications or agents to production.
You have built systems with tool calling, multi-step execution, and evaluations. You understand how the software around a model affects what it can accomplish.
You are a strong programmer in TypeScript or Python, with experience building backend systems and integrating APIs. You’re comfortable owning a feature across the stack.
You think empirically. You define success, run experiments, inspect failures, and use evidence to decide what to build next.
You care deeply about customers and can turn a high-level product idea into a deployed solution. You balance speed with sound engineering judgment.
You take initiative, learn quickly, and collaborate generously. You’re comfortable with ambiguity and make the people around you better.

Compensation Range: $250K - $320K
